title: What is staff minutes per resolved request?
description: Staff minutes per resolved request is the total human time spent getting requests to a confirmed resolution, divided by the number of requests resolved.

summary.question: What is staff minutes per resolved request?
summary.answer: Staff minutes per resolved request is the total human time spent getting requests to a confirmed resolution, divided by the number of requests resolved. It compares a new workflow with your current process on the effort it really takes, including review, corrections and follow-up.

Only requests confirmed as resolved count in the denominator.

scope.covers: Defining and measuring staff minutes per resolved request, with the dealership variant.
scope.excludes: Response-time and satisfaction metrics, and benchmark figures; none are published here.
scope.instead: Writing the rules that decide what software may do on its own is covered in the guide to approval rules.

sections.heading: How is it defined?
paragraphs: Staff minutes per resolved request = total staff minutes spent on the workflow in a period / number of requests resolved in that period.
It answers one question: how much of your team's time does it take to get a request properly finished? A faster first reply that creates rework does not improve it.

sections.heading: What counts as staff time?
list: Writing or reviewing the reply or handoff, including reviewing a prepared draft.
Corrections: fixing a wrong draft, a wrong owner or a wrong detail.
Follow-up messages and calls until the request is resolved.

sections.heading: What counts as resolved?
paragraphs: Agree the definition before you measure. A request is resolved when the person responsible confirms the outcome, for example the test drive or service appointment is confirmed by staff. Requests that were only handed off, are still open or were abandoned do not count as resolved; track them separately as exceptions.

sections.heading: How do you measure it?
list: Write down the definition of resolved and the steps that count as staff time.
Measure the current process over a typical period, before the new workflow goes live.
Measure the new workflow the same way, over a comparable period and request mix.
Report the metric weekly, next to the number of exceptions and reopened requests.
Compare with the baseline at every review.

sections.heading: How does it apply at a dealership?
paragraphs: The same idea adapts to each workflow. For dealership sales and service enquiries, the suggested measure is enquiries with a confirmed next step, read next to the staff effort needed to get there.

sections.heading: What are the common mistakes?
list: Leaving review time out, which makes any automated draft look free.
Counting requests that were handed off but never confirmed as resolved.
Changing the definition of resolved partway through.
Comparing periods with a very different mix of requests.

faq.q: What is staff minutes per resolved request?
faq.a: Staff minutes per resolved request is the total human time spent getting requests to a confirmed resolution, divided by the number of requests resolved. It compares a new workflow with your current process on the effort it really takes, including review, corrections and follow-up.

faq.q: Is a lower number always better?
faq.a: Only if the outcome holds. Read it next to exceptions and reopened requests; a lower number that comes with more reopened requests is not an improvement.

faq.q: Why not just measure response time?
faq.a: Response time shows speed, not effort. A fast reply that needs corrections and extra follow-up can cost more staff time than a slower, complete one.

faq.q: Do we need time-tracking software to measure it?
faq.a: No. A simple log or a timed sample of typical requests is enough, as long as you measure the current process and the new workflow the same way.
